scenes.say: Ever wonder how Kafka splits up work between consumers? And what happens when a consumer drops out?

scenes.label: Group
scenes.sub: A consumer group shares the job of reading a topic.
scenes.say: A consumer group is just a set of consumers sharing the job of reading from a topic.
Kafka assigns each partition to only one consumer in the group at a time. That means each consumer gets its own chunk of data.
If a consumer leaves, Kafka rebalances. The remaining consumer picks up the extra work and reads both partitions.

scenes.question: Does rebalancing always go smoothly?
scenes.right: No, rebalances can cause brief downtime or duplicate processing.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: rebalancing isn't always seamless. It can cause short outages or even duplicate some records.
